beats.caption: Coherent optics link data centres tens to hundreds of km apart
beats.text: An AI campus often spans several buildings or sites, and they must trade data as if they were one cluster. Coherent optics send 400G to 1.6T per wavelength over a single fibre pair for 80 to 1,000+ km, with optical amplifiers every 80 km or so. Ordinary short-reach optics run out of reach after a few kilometres.

beats.caption: Bits ride on phase and amplitude, not just on/off
beats.text: A plain optic turns the light on and off: one bit per symbol. A coherent optic sets the light's phase and amplitude, so each symbol lands on one point of a grid called a constellation. 16QAM has 16 points, so 4 bits per symbol, and two polarisations double it to 8. At ~120 Gbaud that is about 1 Tb/s of raw capacity on one colour.

beats.caption: The transmitter: a laser and nested IQ modulators
beats.text: Inside the module a tunable laser feeds two nested Mach-Zehnder modulators per polarisation: one sets the in-phase part (I), the other the quadrature part (Q), 90 degrees apart. A polarisation rotator and combiner merge the X and Y streams into one fibre. The DSP's DACs drive the modulator electrodes.

beats.caption: The receiver: a local laser and a DSP that undoes the fibre
beats.text: At the far end a second laser, the local oscillator, mixes with the incoming light in a 90-degree hybrid, and balanced photodiodes read out I and Q for each polarisation. A DSP with fast ADCs then reverses chromatic dispersion and polarisation drift and applies error correction, so smeared pulses become clean symbols. That DSP is the hardest and most power-hungry chip in the module.

beats.caption: 400ZR and 800ZR put coherent into a switch port
beats.text: Coherent used to need large line-card systems. 400ZR and 800ZR pluggables shrink it to a QSFP-DD or OSFP module that plugs straight into a switch, at about 15-30 W each. Ciena (CIEN) leads line systems, Marvell (MRVL) and Cisco (CSCO, via Acacia) make coherent DSPs and modules, and Coherent (COHR) and Lumentum (LITE) supply lasers and modulators.
